Doc comments are misplaced or contradict the code. summary.ts:79-92 is the JSDoc 'Schema for the results feed', but a second JSDoc (93) follows it, so it attaches to the COMMIT_SHA regex at 94 and not to runSchema at 119. relativeTime.ts:3-4 stacks two JSDoc blocks. The first describes `formatter` at line 10 but attaches to DAYS_PER_MONTH. RunList.tsx:92-96 says 'The title above still truncates, deliberately'. titleStyle at 59-76 wraps with overflowWrap:'anywhere', and its own comment at 59-64 says truncation was removed. RunHeader.tsx:107 checks `commitUrl !== null && run.commit !== null`, but gatedCommitUrl (runLinks.ts:26-28) already returns null exactly when commit is null. RunList.tsx:242 and RunHeader.tsx:91 test `deployUrl !== ''`, and safeUrl (design-system/safeHttpUrl.ts) never returns an empty string. RunList.tsx:202-203 and 212-213 repeat the same `closest('a')` guard in two handlers.

I found no classes and no layers built for features nobody asked for. The thin wrappers are Page.tsx:28-55, ThemeToggle.tsx, Breadcrumbs.tsx, shell/Header.tsx, shell/MobileDrawer.tsx and lib/useDocumentMeta.ts:22-24. Each one binds this app's tokens or origin to a shared design-system component, and the pages use them on several routes (all 7 pages render Page). FeedStatus.tsx has 3 note components, and Home and RunDetail both use them. Home.tsx:25-65 splits into HomeBody and Home, and RunDetail.tsx:52-118 splits into RunDetailView and RunDetail. Both splits let tests inject state, and production uses both halves. The one borderline case is runLinks.ts:26-28 gatedCommitUrl. It is a one-line ternary with a single production caller (RunHeader.tsx:68), and it forces the redundant check at RunHeader.tsx:107. It is tested and sits next to its sibling gateResultUrl, so I did not fail the rule on it alone.

useDocumentMeta.ts:15 hardcodes `SITE_ORIGIN = 'https://redanvil-dashboard.pages.dev'`. shell/constants.ts:5 already exports the same value as DASHBOARD_URL, and Footer.tsx:44 uses it. functions/api/health.ts:8 hardcodes the origin a third time. summary.ts:102-106 gatedCommit narrows provenance with hand-written `typeof` checks, right beside the Zod runSchema. The comment at summary.ts:82-87 says typeof chains were replaced with Zod after this exact rule failed, yet this function still uses one. A `z.object({commit: z.string().regex(COMMIT_SHA)})` with `.catch(null)` would fit the schema at line 135. The transport does use the shared requestJson (useRuns.ts:62), and links go through safeUrl and SafeExternalLink. The duplicated origin constant and the hand narrowing are still new code written where shared or library code already exists.

Not verified. I was told not to run git, so I could not inspect the diff or compare its size to a ticket, and a PASS needs evidence. The only view of the change is the HEAD commit subject, 'fix(dashboard): no double slug decode, no duplicate scroll reset or linkify wrapper'. That subject bundles three unrelated fixes into one commit. Source comments also narrate project history that no behavior needs. summary.ts:82-88 recounts a prior judge verdict, and RunList.tsx:59-64, RunList.tsx:78-81 and KpiStrip.tsx:37-41 recount measurement history. A diff scoped to one ticket would not add that. Nothing I could read shows the diff stayed within its ticket.

This app ships no authentication surface, so there is no guard to stub: functions/ contains only the health endpoint. No auth-named function returns an unconditional truthy value and there is no TODO-auth marker.

The HEAD fix for double slug decoding (RunDetail.tsx:102-105) has no assertion. RunDetail.test.ts renders only RunDetailBody and RunDetailView (lines 25 and 77), never the routed RunDetail component. No unit, browser or e2e test opens a slug that contains an encoded '%'. tests/runs.spec.ts:156-164 only clicks a plain slug. Nothing asserts the per-route metadata RunDetail builds at RunDetail.tsx:108-115 (title, description and encoded path). useDocumentMeta.test.ts:11-14 checks only typeof and arity. RunList.tsx:203 makes the card ignore clicks on its nested links. No test clicks the deploy or title link to confirm the card handler stays out of the way. RunList.browser.test.ts:64-70 clicks only the status icon. Coverage is good elsewhere: useRuns.test.ts:36-122 covers every fetchRuns branch, and Home.test.ts and RunDetail.test.ts:88-147 cover every view state.

Several tests check implementation details or presence instead of behavior. useDocumentMeta.test.ts:12-13 asserts `typeof useDocumentMeta === 'function'` and `useDocumentMeta.length === 1`. That says nothing about the title, description or canonical tag the hook sets. runFixture.test.ts:4-30 tests a test-only fixture with presence checks such as `rules.length toBeGreaterThan(0)` (line 10) and `deployUrl toMatch(/^https/)` (line 12). linkify.test.ts:7-8 builds its own copy of the ContentSections call instead of rendering ContentSections. It then asserts `nodes.length toBeGreaterThan(1)` (line 19) and reads React element internals, `props.children` and `c.type === 'a'` (lines 24-29), instead of rendered output. en.test.ts:239 asserts the literal glyph '☾'. useRuns.test.ts does it right: it stubs fetch at the network boundary and asserts the returned state for every error branch. The arity and presence tests above still fail the rule.

Every page returns a short list of named components, with no inline markup or style objects. Home.tsx:44-51 renders Page around an optional AlertNote and RunsOverview. Home owns the useRuns state and the query (62-64) and passes both down. RunDetail.tsx:28-36 renders RunHeader, IterationHistory and RuleBreakdown. RunDetail owns the slug and the feed state (102-106). About, Terms, Privacy and Contact (lines 15-17) each render Page around ContentSections. NotFound.tsx:26-29 renders Page around StatusNote and BackToRunsLink. One small point: HomeBody (Home.tsx:28-51) and RunDetailView (RunDetail.tsx:55-92) repeat the `<Page title=...>` wrapper in every state branch instead of wrapping once. Each branch still reads as named components.

Every screen defines loading, error, empty and partial states, and no failure renders as a clean empty success. useRuns.ts:40-46 turns a feed with only malformed rows into an error, not an empty list. A feed with some bad rows becomes a partial state. useRuns.ts:60-67 turns every thrown failure into an error state: a bad HTTP status, a non-array body, a timeout or a transport error. describeFetchError (25-31) gives the timeout its own message. While the feed loads, Home.tsx:28-34 shows a LoadingNote marked aria-busy. On failure, Home.tsx:36-42 shows an AlertNote. On a partial feed, Home.tsx:46-48 shows a notice above the runs it could read. RunsOverview.tsx:26-47 separates 'no runs yet' from 'no runs match this search'. RunDetail.tsx:55-92 handles loading, error with a way back, found, partial-not-found and not-found. Inside a run, IterationHistory.tsx:81-84 and RuleBreakdown.tsx:64-67 show explicit empty notes. Tests assert all of these branches: useRuns.test.ts:55-122, Home.test.ts:40-106 and RunDetail.test.ts:57-147.
